original_value: Multivariate data sets are common in various application areas, such as wireless sensor networks (WSNs) and DNA analysis. A robust mechanism is required to compute their similarity indexes regardless of the environment and problem domain. This study describes the usefulness of a non-metric-based approach (i.e., longest common subsequence) in computing similarity indexes. Several non-metric-based algorithms are available in the literature, the most robust and reliable one is the dynamic programming-based technique. However, dynamic programming-based techniques are considered inefficient, particularly in the context of multivariate data sets. Furthermore, the classical approaches are not powerful enough in scenarios with multivariate data sets, sensor data or when the similarity indexes are extremely high or low. To address this issue, we propose an efficient algorithm to measure the similarity indexes of multivariate data sets using a non-metric-based methodology. The proposed algorithm performs exceptionally well on numerous multivariate data sets compared with the classical dynamic programming-based algorithms. The performance of the algorithms is evaluated on the basis of several benchmark data sets and a dynamic multivariate data set, which is obtained from a WSN deployed in the Ghulam Ishaq Khan (GIK) Institute of Engineering Sciences and Technology. Our evaluation suggests that the proposed algorithm can be approximately 39.9% more efficient than its counterparts for various data sets in terms of computational time.

result.paraphrase: Multivariate data sets are widely used in many application domains, including wireless sensor networks (WSNs) and DNA analysis. Computing similarity indexes in any environment or problem domain requires a robust mechanism. This study highlights the value of a non-metric approach, namely the longest common subsequence, for computing similarity indexes. Although several non-metric algorithms appear in the literature, the dynamic programming-based technique is regarded as the most robust and reliable. Even so, dynamic programming methods are inefficient, especially for multivariate data sets. In addition, classical approaches are not sufficiently effective for multivariate data sets, sensor data, or cases where similarity indexes are extremely high or low. To overcome this limitation, we present an efficient algorithm for measuring the similarity indexes of multivariate data sets using a non-metric methodology. Compared with classical dynamic programming-based algorithms, the proposed algorithm performs exceptionally well on many multivariate data sets. Its performance is assessed using several benchmark data sets and a dynamic multivariate data set collected from a WSN deployed at the Ghulam Ishaq Khan (GIK) Institute of Engineering Sciences and Technology. The evaluation indicates that, in terms of computational time, the proposed algorithm can be about 39.9% more efficient than comparable methods across various data sets.
